notes: Ground truth for the review-tests prompt. Project has zero test files and no test runner declared; the eval focuses on (a) flagging the absence as the dominant finding and (b) naming the highest-risk untested modules so the recommendation is actionable.

findings.summary: Project declares no test runner (no jest, vitest, mocha, node:test) and no `test` script. There is no path for CI to run tests at all.
findings.evidence: package.json scripts: {dev, watch:main, watch:renderer, build, dist, typecheck}. No `test`, no test-runner dependency. No jest.config.* / vitest.config.* in the tree.
findings.recommendation: Add vitest as a devDependency (works for both main/Node and renderer code via jsdom), set `"test": "vitest run"` and `"test:watch": "vitest"`, then commit a minimal smoke test for the highest-risk module first (see TST-002).

findings.summary: ELM327Commander has zero tests — it owns the entire serial protocol state machine (send chain, prompt detection, timeout handling, PID response parsing). Bugs here corrupt every reading shown to the user.
findings.evidence: No *.test.ts / *.spec.ts file references ELM327Commander; the only exerciser of the parsing logic is the live serial path.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for parsePIDResponse (header detection, multi-ECU truncation, malformed-hex rejection), the send-chain ordering (two concurrent send() calls must serialize), and the timeout path (late bytes from a previous command must not corrupt the next reply).

findings.summary: OBDProtocolManager has zero tests — it owns DTC parsing (Mode 03/07/0A) and the supported-PID bitmask discovery. A parse bug emits wrong DTC codes to the assistant and the user.
findings.evidence: discoverSupportedPIDs() shifts a 4-byte bitmask into PIDs; parseDTCResponse() bit-packs the type nibble. Neither path is exercised by any test.
findings.recommendation: Add table-driven tests over known-good fixtures: each official Mode 03/07/0A example from SAE J1979 → expected DTC list; each bitmask example from ELM327 docs → expected PID set.

findings.summary: PID decode formulas are pure functions (trim, tempF, rpm, maf, volt1, …) — easiest possible tests, zero exist. A miscoded formula shows wrong readings to the user with no warning.
findings.evidence: pidCatalog.ts exports ~14 pure decode helpers. None are tested. Several have non-obvious factors (rpm = (a*256+b)/4, trim = ((a-128)/128)*100).
findings.recommendation: One-line parametric test per helper: assert decode([fixture_bytes]) === expected_value for at least the boundary cases (min, max, midpoint, the known-good example value).

findings.summary: Even if tests existed, there is no CI pipeline to run them (no .github/workflows, no .gitlab-ci.yml, no .circleci). The only quality gate the codebase enforces is `tsc --noEmit`.
findings.evidence: Absence of CI config; the `typecheck` script is the sole automation-friendly check.
findings.recommendation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on PR: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test`. Block merge on red.

findings.summary: The ELM327 simulator and the real-device path share NO common test. Drift between simulator encoding and real-device decoding is the most likely source of silent regressions because dev work happens against the simulator.
findings.evidence: elm327Simulator.respond() encodes responses; ELM327Commander.parsePIDResponse() decodes them. No round-trip test asserts simulator.respond(pid) decoded back equals the simulator's internal state.
findings.recommendation: Add one round-trip test per PID: for each entry in PID_MAP, feed simulator's response into parsePIDResponse + the decode helper, assert it round-trips the simulator's internal state within tolerance.
